newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African money mkt taking high shortage in stride.
newsitem.headline: S.African money mkt taking high shortage in stride.

text.p: South Africa's daily money market shortage remains stubbornly above 10 billion rand but the market is taking the squeeze in its stride with short-term rates holding steady, dealers said on Friday.

Leading banks quoted three-month NCD rates unchanged at between 17.25-17.50 percent on Friday while 90-day BA rates were also unchanged at 16.60-16.85 percent. Call money was also steady around 17.00 percent.

The average rate for three-month Treasury bills at this week's auction was seen little changed from last week with dealers polled forecasting a rate between 16.22 and 16.34 percent from 16.26 percent.
Traders said they expected the shortage to move sideways or trend slightly lower in the coming days after its rise to 10.444 billion rand on Thursday from 10.131 billion rand on Wednesday.
"I think the shortage will come down a bit but the authorities may try to keep it around 9.5 billion. It doesn't look like they want to take the pressure off for the moment," said one.
Dealers put the latest increase down to forex outflows from the Reserve Bank but said the increase should not cause undue alarm.
"It's small outflows. The Reserve Bank has been flexing its muscles a little bit, ostensibly to support the rand, but it's not a train smash," said one market trader.
"The perception among market players is that the shortage will trend sideways in the coming days with call rates remaining confident."
He noted that call rates had come down 1.25 percentage points since their peak over the Christmas period, despite the continuing high money market shortage.

At the long end of the market the yield on the R150 bond shrugged off the disappointing money market shortage with the issue last yielding 15.57 percent, more than 10 basis points off its morning low and compared to 15.62 percent at 1400 GMT on Thursday.

Dealers said they remained hopeful that money market rates would ease further in the coming months, paving the way for a bank rate cut around mid-year. Bank rate currently stands at 17 percent with prime at 20.25 percent.
